messages.subject: functional response
parts:
Hi, 

I am working with my internship tutor on an R-Shiny application, based on the DEB_euler and DEB fonctions, whose goal is to simulate aquaculture waste (food, faeces...).

As we are dealing with farmed fishes, we were wondering how we could model the different practices of fish farmers regarding the management of fish diets. Indeed, farmers can overfeed or underfeed animals according to their development stage in order to improve growth performances. 

Our question is the following:  as it refers to the equation f(X)=X/(K+X) can the functional response f in the DEB_euler fonction be larger than 1 ? Or should we model an overfed individual with f=1 ?

For now, we only found about f < 1  in the scientific literature and implemented it into our farm model with no difficulty. However, we can't find any results based on f > 1.

Thank you for your time. 

Kind regards, 

Léanne

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: functional response
parts:
Hi Léanne,

Good question. You can make f > 1, and I've seen this done in some parameter estimation routines,  but that is the same as increasing the maximum specific assimilation rate parameter {p_Am}. So it will mean your fish will grow bigger. It won't become fatter for the same size (i.e., storing an excess of e.g. fat).

All the best,
Mike
